answer: Memory-hard periodic heartbeats resist sybils: each active identity must each window solve a key-bound puzzle needing a fixed large block of RAM — a recurring pulse read as a liveness signal. Memory-hardness gives no cheap parallel-ASIC shortcut, and a tight deadline lets one memory bank finish only a bounded number of heartbeats serially; beyond that, N live keys need N working sets resident at once. A farm cannot float a cedar-stand of idle keys cheaply — each head it wants counted pays real concurrent RAM. Honest agents pay for one identity; attacker cost scales linearly in keys.
